\chapter{Synthesis --- Carrying a Conversation}
\label{ch:sintesis-reportar}
\hlchaptermodality{217}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can report a whole exchange to somebody who was not there.}

I can report a whole exchange to somebody who was not there.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[(synthesis)]{(synthesis)}

\label{lesson:ES-C57-sintesis-reportar}



\begin{quote}
Here is a very short conversation. Two people, four lines.

\begin{quote}
— \emph{¿Dónde trabajas?} — \emph{Trabajo en casa.} — \emph{¿Estás cansado?} — \emph{Sí.}
\end{quote}

You were there. Somebody else was not.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Carry it across, line by line. Every line needs a joint, and the joint is different every time.

The first line was a question with an asking word. (\emph{Preguntó dónde trabajaba}.)

The second was a statement. (\emph{Dijo que trabajaba en casa}.)

The third was a yes-or-no question. (\emph{Preguntó si estaba cansado}.)
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} all three reports, one after another, without stopping
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read your three sentences back and name what is \textbf{not} in them. (No question marks — and not one verb left in the present.)

Four lines of live speech went in; one steady account came out. What is new is not that you said something in Spanish — it is that you \textbf{carried} somebody else's words to a person who was not there, and marked every seam where they stopped being your own.
\end{tcolorbox}
